Kaisa Laine
kaisa.laine@mail.example | +358 00 000 0103

Education

Experience

Signal Processing Engineer
Aurinko Avionics, Espoo
2008 – present

- Contributed to signal processing subsystems for airborne radar and optical instrument products across multiple EORA-contracted programmes
- Participated in flight qualification and acceptance testing campaigns for two airborne instrument payloads delivered to EORA (2012 and 2018)
- All technical documentation, design reviews, and customer communication conducted in English as the company's working language for international space programmes

Projects

**Phased-array beamforming for airborne SAR receiver** (2014 – 2017)
Designed a beamforming algorithm for the receive chain of an 8-element X-band synthetic aperture radar antenna. The work covered sidelobe suppression, null placement for interference rejection, and beam-steering angle optimisation for off-nadir imaging. Implemented in MATLAB for prototype validation, then delivered the design specification for firmware integration.

**Embedded DSP for optical-instrument readout** (2018 – 2020)
Wrote embedded DSP firmware in C for a TI TMS320C6678 multi-core processor, handling real-time data reduction from an optical detector array operating at 200 MS/s. The firmware implemented baseline subtraction, noise blanking, and packet framing for downlink, all within a 5 W power envelope.

**Post-flight data processing toolkit** (2020 – present)
Built and maintained a Python-based data processing toolkit for post-flight analysis of instrument telemetry. Handles data ingestion, calibration correction, and quick-look product generation. Maintained with pytest and used across Aurinko's Espoo and Oulu offices. Includes a CLI documented for non-developer users.

**CubeSat imager signal-chain design** (2022 – 2023)
Designed a miniaturised signal chain for a CubeSat imager payload, drawing directly on the signal theory, statistical methods, and numerical analysis foundations of my Engineering Physics MSc from Kallavesi. The design covered detector front-end through A/D conversion, noise reduction, and lossless compression.

**Oulu facility integration support** (2023 – 2024)
Provided six months of on-site signal processing support at Aurinko's Oulu facility during integration and environmental testing of a multi-spectral sensor payload. Close day-to-day coordination with the Oulu-based systems engineering team.

Skills

Signal processing algorithm design, embedded firmware (C, TI DSPs), Python, MATLAB, airborne instrument systems, SAR processing, data reduction, optical detector readout
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Remote-sensing instruments are what I have spent my career building, and Kaikuvaara is the company in Finland that does this work best. That is the short version of why I am applying.

I have been at Aurinko Avionics since 2008, working on signal processing for airborne and spaceborne instrument payloads. Over that time I have designed beamforming algorithms for SAR receivers, written embedded DSP firmware in C for optical-instrument readout at 200 MS/s, and built a Python data processing toolkit that the analysis team uses across two offices. The work I find most compelling is the transition from algorithm design to flight-qualified hardware — the moment when you discover which of your design assumptions actually hold when the instrument is running on a real platform, collecting real data, under real thermal and power constraints.

I have been part of two EORA-contracted airborne instrument programmes that went through full flight qualification, in 2012 and 2018. Those experiences shaped how I think about instrument signal processing. The constraints of a flight platform — fixed power budgets, radiation tolerance, no opportunity for a firmware update once the instrument is airborne — force you to be very deliberate about what goes into the design and very thorough about how you test it. The most recent programme involved an optical instrument payload, and it reinforced something I had already learned from the 2012 radar campaign: the hardest problems in instrument signal processing are the ones you do not see coming until the real data arrives.

What draws me to Kaikuvaara specifically is the focus. Aurinko is an avionics company that happens to build instruments as one of several product lines; Kaikuvaara is an instruments company. That difference shows up in how much depth and continuity the instrument engineering group gets, and in the career development available to someone who wants to stay technical. I am not looking for a management path. I want to keep designing signal processing systems for instruments that fly, and I think Kaikuvaara is the best place in Finland to do that.

If you are looking for someone who can step in and contribute across algorithm design and embedded implementation, with a real understanding of what flight-qualified instrument engineering requires, I would welcome the chance to discuss it.

Kaisa Laine

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
